content:
This is a sign of success
It doesn’t look like success.
Not when you get attacked every week like I do.
Last week was a record, 8 different people sent abusive emails and LinkedIn messages.

This was the nicest one.

When you succeed, people make up lies about you.
They will come after you in different ways that are unexpected.
They set up fake profiles and want you to react because they have nothing else going on.

When you get attacked on social media for sharing success or writing a genuine post, please remember this about haters.

1.    Their lives are miserable.
2.    It says more about their lack of intelligence than anything else.
3.    They spent time creating a fake profile to attack you. How sad is that.

The old saying “It’s not what happens, it’s how you react to it,” is more important than ever in 2026.

✅ Always improve yourself
✅ Support others when you can
✅ Never stop learning
✅ Kindness is a superpower
✅ Most importantly, you don’t have to react to everything
personaInterest: Maintaining a positive online presence and dealing with negativity
keyTakeaway: The target persona is likely experiencing rapid growth and success, but struggling with managing online harassment and negativity, presenting an opportunity for solutions focused on social media management and online reputation protection.

content:
Don’t tell prospects what to do
It annoys them.
I learned this the hard way.

I would slide into DMs and, with pure sincerity, tell prospects what they were doing wrong.
Most ignored me.
A few said thank you
No meetings took place, no money was generated.

✅ So I look carefully at the industry they work in

✅ I do my research and share insights that help them progress to show some kind of understanding. That builds trust.

✅ I make it personal so they know it’s not another generic copy and paste. That helps you stand out.

✅ I follow-up instead of saying what many people do “Following-up is beneath me” or “Following-up is too salesly.”

✅ I also make sure my signature doesn't take up half the email like in this image

Now only some people ignore me 😃 

I have more conversations, more meetings and more clients won this way.

It’s easy to tell people what to do.

It’s hard work to make an effort, research, be personal and generate revenue.

Choose the right one.
keyTakeaway: Personalized, research-driven sales outreach efforts can significantly improve conversation rates and client acquisition.

content:
Do business like Harry Styles
I took my daughter and stepdaughter to see Harry Styles on Friday night.
(my eldest stepdaughter is 4 months pregnant, so didn’t make the trip)

My free time is spent going to rock concerts, not popular pop. This was done to make my family happy. 

On a few occasions during the concert, Harry said how truly grateful he was that everyone had taken time out of their busy lives to spend with him. It wasn’t a quick exchange. It was a good 30 -40 seconds per person in a crowd of about 80,000 people.

He asked people where they were from. He showed genuine interest and thanked them for making the journey.

He moved around the stadium on several occasions to make sure he made eye contact with the crowd. They loved every moment.

To paraphrase what Harry said “The love and energy in this stadium tonight is amazing. Please take that with you and share it with the world.”

Having just had our honeymoon, I was reluctant to take a trip to London. The price of flights, accommodation, tickets, taxis, food and drink in London, is insane. It was worth it. 

✅ Make your customer feel special
✅ Ask them questions
✅ Listen
✅ Care
✅ Don’t rush.

PS Love conquers hate, jealousy and every other bad emotion.
personaInterest: Delivering exceptional customer service and building meaningful relationships
keyTakeaway: Prioritize making customers feel special by actively listening, showing genuine interest, and caring about their needs to foster loyalty and drive business growth.

content:
Client indecision. The silent killer in business

You know how it feels. You have a great conversation, the client nods along, asks all the right questions, and then… nothing. Or “Let me get back to you next quarter.”

Here’s what I’ve learned after 31 years in sales: Indecision isn’t always about your offer or price.

It’s about risk, uncertainty, and fear of making the wrong move.

1. Don’t let indecision go unchallenged. If a client says they need more time, ask what’s holding them back.

2. Simply asking “Is there anything specific you’d like more clarity on?” opens up the real conversation.

3. Follow up like a pro. Most people give up after one message. The best clients often need six or more follow-ups. Because they’re busy, not because they’re not interested.

4. Stay positive and confident. Indecision tests your patience, but your confidence in your offer is what reassures your client. Don’t “hope” it will work for them—show them how it already has for others.

5. Create urgency. People need a reason to act now, not someday. Remind them what they stand to lose by waiting—lost revenue, missed opportunities, or letting the competition get ahead.

Indecision happens.

Address it, learn from it, and help clients move forward with clarity. If you’re facing client indecision right now, you’re not alone and yes, you can turn it into action.

PS I didn’t have an image to go with this, so here’s a picture of me delivering sales training to a client.
personaInterest: Overcoming client indecision and closing deals
keyTakeaway: Sales representatives can turn client indecision into action by addressing risk and uncertainty, creating urgency, and following up persistently with confidence in their offer.

content:
I was sold to on my honeymoon

The best people were the waiters and waitresses on the cruise.
Rachel had a Bride baseball cap on and that was a talking point.
At breakfast, waiters told me their favourites songs by Aerosmith, ACDC or Bon Jovi, depending on what top I was wearing.

They got tipped well. Paying attention matters. Talking to me without looking at your mobile matters. 

On the cruise ship, the rest of the selling was relentless.

The worst was when I went to buy diamond earrings for Rachel. The salesman talked for 5 minutes. Didn’t ask a single question. I thanked him and said I would think about it.

He offered me a 20% discount.
I said no.

He told me his favourite people in the world were Scottish.
I explained I was Irish 🤭 

The next day we landed in San Juan, Puerto Rico and visited a jewellery shop
The salesman here took his time.
Asked questions.
Listened.
Told me his family story, which was lovely.

He spent 30 minutes with Rachel trying on different earrings. He said there was no rush and to take our time.

When he asked Rachel for her favourite cocktail, she said “pina colada.”

And he recommended the best pina colada place in town.

Afterwards, we returned and I bought the diamond earrings which were MORE EXPENSIVE than the cruise ship.

Be human. Connect with people. In a world obsessed with AI, soft skills matter more than ever in sales.
personaInterest: The importance of human connection and soft skills in sales
keyTakeaway: Emphasize the value of personal connection and active listening in sales pitches to build trust and close deals.
